title: Does Code Quality Still Matter? It Depends on This — Max Kanat-Alexander, Capital One
talk_summary: Max Kanat-Alexander argues all software success reduces to understanding the system and executing on that understanding, and that code quality only matters insofar as it preserves understandable structure for future modification. He introduces a 'disposable vs durable' spectrum (judged by consequences of failure, replacement cost, dependencies, maintenance cost) and argues the highest-leverage move is making engineering rigor cheap via standardization, inward-flow tooling, easy testing, and maximum strictness.

takeaways.what_they_do: Judge software on four factors (consequences of failure, cost of replacement, dependencies, cost of maintenance) and apply engineering rigor proportional to durability rather than uniformly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: In the future, we will apply engineering rigor to the degree of disposability of the software.

takeaways.technique: Inward-flow tooling: rigor that runs automatically and reliably
takeaways.what_they_do: Make quality tooling run without the programmer choosing or configuring it — fast, low false-positive, 'feels free' — so it can be applied even to disposable code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: inward flow tooling is tooling that just occurs. The programmer doesn't have to choose to run it.

takeaways.what_they_do: Turn all lint rules to maximum up front and never compromise, accepting occasional false positives to avoid a large backlog of accumulated issues and repeated debates.
Eliminate whole classes of choice (languages, frameworks, protocols) so tooling and rigor don't have to be rebuilt per stack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do standardization because it removes possibilities... it just reduces the cost of rigor.

takeaways.technique: In-memory fakes for services, generated by agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Have each service ship an in-memory fake so tests are fast and deterministic without deep testing expertise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everybody would provide in-memory fake versions of their services... Guess what? The coding agent can do that.

takeaways.technique: Isolated disposable environments to contain risk
takeaways.what_they_do: Constrain deployments to environments with no customer data/PII and no inbound production API calls, making everything there disposable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can only deploy to this environment that has access to only your data. No customer data, no personally identifiable information
